messages:
sasha: Proposal — add a zone-aware preemptible "burst" nodepool for Dedicated GPU clusters. Idea: use preemptible GPUs in a specific AZ for low-cost batch/burst workloads, but prefer same-zone allocations for latency-sensitive tenant pods and fail over to hosted if local preemptibles are unavailable. Looking for feedback on isolation and autoscaler changes.
kevin: sounds promising. main concern is noisy neighbors when preemptible nodes get reclaimed mid-inference run. How do we ensure tenant isolation and avoid eviction storms? :thinking: 
anya: two quick ideas: 1) label namespaces for "burst-eligible" so regular tenant namespaces never get scheduled there; 2) use PodDisruptionBudgets + graceful checkpointing for long-running jobs.
jamie: agree with namespace labels. We should also ensure we don't mix preemptible GPUs with reserved pools in the same nodepool (taints + tolerations). Otherwise kube-scheduler might still mix things up.
sasha: exactly — plan is nodepool taint: gpu-burst=preemptible:NoSchedule plus a toleration for burst namespaces. For tenant isolation: non-burst namespaces have a nodeSelector: pool in (dedicated, hosted).
kevin: autoscaler implications? cluster-autoscaler will scale down preemptible pool aggressively; we want a small min-size to avoid constant churn during spikes. Maybe configurable minBurstReplicas. Also need zone-aware CA so one AZ running out doesn't wipe capacity across the cluster.
anya: here's a sample CA config snippet I was experimenting with:
```yaml
expander: least-waste
scaleDown: true
maxNodeProvisionTime: 20m
nodeGroups:
  - name: gpu-burst-az-a
    minSize: 1
    maxSize: 8
    labels:
      topology.kubernetes.io/zone: us-west1-a
    taints:
      - key: gpu-burst
        value: preemptible
        effect: NO_SCHEDULE
```
jamie: add a policy to prefer same-zone scheduling for pods with nodeAffinity to reduce cross-AZ traffic — important for model shard locality and KV cache hits.
ml-ops-bot: NOTE: when a preemptible node is reclaimed, any running GPU workload is terminated immediately. Recommend short checkpoint intervals (<= 30s) for training/batching jobs.
kevin: two more failure modes: 1) autoscaler evicts pod while it's still warming GPU caches -> significant tail latency; 2) scheduler spreads replicas across zones but autoscaler scales one zone down. Need a reconciliation loop to detect such imbalance and either migrate pods or spin up hosted fallback.
sasha: agree. Proposal: implement a controller that watches burst nodepools and maintains a zone imbalance metric. If imbalance > threshold and preemptible capacity < X, create a hosted fallback replica in the same region with a lower-QPS routing tag. Routing trick: attach route tags so API layer can prefer local preemptible instances but fallback to hosted with tag "burst-fallback".
anya: routing tags are good. But we need strong SLAs for private customers — can't silently fallback without observability. Add a cost/latency signal to Console to show % of requests served by preemptible vs hosted.
jamie: also we must be careful with KMS/HSM-backed tenants on Private: preemptible nodes might not be allowed for certain customers. Add a tenant label `allow_preemptible: "true"` and block scheduling otherwise.
kevin: cost model question: how much cheaper? if preemptible is 60% cheaper but reliability drops, teams might overuse it. We should expose an estimated per-token cost delta and an ongoing alert when cost-savings correlate with quality regressions.
sasha: yes — Redwood Optimize should ingest signals (latency, error rate, cost delta) and recommend when to toggle burst eligibility per workload.
infra-oncall: FYI, I just saw a cross-zone CNI spike when we tested cross-AZ bursting last week — manifests as 20–30ms extra p95 for KV. Suggest we add an e2e perf test to the PR.
jamie: +1 on e2e. Also add an emergency failover annotation so oncall can block preemptible scheduling for a tenant if we detect network instability.
kevin: operational runbook thoughts:
- how to roll back if burst nodepool causes evictions: taint the pool, drain with --pod-selector for burst namespaces, scale down to 0.
- verify autoscaler calms down by checking Event spikes and CA scale events.
- notify tenants via Slack channel and console alert.
sasha: I'll draft a RFC with config examples, autoscaler knobs, and the controller responsibilities. Plan to prototype in staging (us-west1-a and -b) next sprint.
ml-ops-bot: TODO created: RFC-2093 "zone-aware preemptible burst policy" assigned to sasha, reviewers: kevin, anya, jamie.
kevin: lgtm for prototype. Let's include a short demo app that shows fallback routing and cost/latency dashboards.
anya: I'll add checkpointing helpers and a sample K8s manifest for burst-tolerant jobs.
jamie: will take the e2e perf tests.
sasha: thanks all. tagging @infra-oncall for schedule — want to run the first test Thursday 09:00 PT.
infra-oncall: ack. I'll reserve the staging clusters and post the test run link before Wed EOD. :thumbsup:
